correctness.rationale: For k>=2 and precisely k+1 distinct ordered agents on the real line, the nearest-facility social optimum is min adjacent gap m by pigeonhole and triangle inequality. Product-Gap selection omits one position; for the product P of k adjacent gaps, omission weights are P/g1 for the first, P(1/g_{i-1}+1/g_i) internally, P/g_k for the last, total Z=2PΣ1/g_j. The omitted agent alone pays its nearest adjacent gap, giving the exact expected social-cost identity [k+1+Σ min(g_j,g_{j+1})/max(g_j,g_{j+1})]/[2Σ 1/g_j]. At m=g_t, set h_j=m/g_j,A=Σ_{j≠t} h_j>0; adjacent ratio terms are bounded by adjacent h and all others by 1, leading ratio≤(2k-1+A)/(2(1+A))<k-1/2. Gap family g1=eps,g2..k=1 tends to the bound, never reaches for positive m. Independent exact rational direct weighted-selected-subset enumerations on 350 profiles across k=2..8 reproduced normalization, identity and strict bound.
residual_risks: Only one-dimensional additive distance cost, the specified Product-Gap selection, exactly k+1 agents, positive m. Does not assert strategyproofness or an unrestricted many-agent approximation ratio.
